data.title: Famciclovir
data.summary: IV Antivirals — Anti-herpes · Diacetyl ester prodrug of penciclovir (guanosine analogue)
data.body:
_Oral · IV Antivirals — Anti-herpes_

**Class:** Diacetyl ester prodrug of penciclovir (guanosine analogue)

## Mechanism of action
- Converted to penciclovir in the gut wall and liver
- Penciclovir is phosphorylated by viral thymidine kinase, then by host kinases, to penciclovir triphosphate, which inhibits viral DNA polymerase
- Not an obligate chain terminator (unlike acyclovir), but stays inside infected cells much longer (intracellular half-life 7–20 h)

## Pharmacokinetics
- Bioavailability about 77%
- Plasma half-life about 2 h, but long intracellular half-life → less frequent dosing
- Renal excretion — reduce dose in renal impairment

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Herpes zoster (start within 72 h)
- Genital herpes: first episode, recurrences, suppression
- Herpes labialis (single dose)
- Recurrent HSV in HIV

## Dose & formulations
- Herpes zoster: 500 mg three times daily × 7 days
- First-episode genital herpes: 250 mg three times daily × 7–10 days
- Recurrent genital herpes: 1 g twice daily for 1 day (or 125 mg twice daily × 5 days)
- Suppression: 250 mg twice daily
- Herpes labialis: 1500 mg single dose
- HIV, recurrent HSV: 500 mg twice daily × 7 days

## Adverse effects
- Headache, nausea, diarrhoea
- Confusion in the elderly (rare)

## Contraindications
- Hypersensitivity to famciclovir or penciclovir

## Drug interactions
- Probenecid may raise penciclovir levels
- Few clinically important interactions

## Monitoring
- Renal function for dose adjustment

## Pregnancy & lactation
Old FDA category B; limited human data — acyclovir and valacyclovir are preferred in pregnancy.

## Viva points
- Prodrug of penciclovir; long intracellular half-life
- Cross-resistance with acyclovir (both need viral thymidine kinase)
- Single-day treatment options for herpes labialis and recurrent genital herpes

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.11; Khopkar ch.3. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
